issues.issue: The replacement text reads "For up to NA days at each place to which the property has been taken," which states no period and cannot be applied as a coverage term.
It purports to delete and replace the ninety-day temporary-location period in Form RM1002 A.17.b(1), so the policy contains two irreconcilable statements of how long removed property stays insured.

The extension grants penalty coverage by "modifying" Form RM1001 C.8.b(2), which excludes fines or damages "for penalties of any nature," and the same exclusion is repeated in the Extra Expense exclusions at D.3.e(2), which the endorsement does not touch.

Payment requires that the insured "be found to be legally liable" for the penalties, without saying by whom or in what forum, while paragraph 3 disclaims any duty to defend the very proceeding that would produce such a finding.

"The policy deductible" is not a single figure: Declarations G. states $10,000 but marks the box directing the reader to Form RM1115, which lists several category deductibles and none for contract penalties.
The definition says the TRIA criteria "include the following" and then lists two, so the list is non-exhaustive and the boundary of a certified act as used in the exclusion is left open.

The fire buy-back gives the full limit only in the states on the endorsement's Schedule, which does not include Kansas, so every scheduled location in this policy falls under the $1,000,000 alternative — a result at odds with the $65,808,311 blanket limit on the Declarations.

"The reasonable extra costs of temporary repair to property or of expediting the permanent repair ... whichever is less" leaves it unclear whether the comparison is between the two categories of cost or between cost and some other measure.

The clause redefines "extra expenses" locally for hazardous substance cleanup, while "extra expense" is a defined policy term in Form RM1007 L. carrying a different meaning; which meaning governs is left to be worked out.

Payment is to be determined "in accordance with the valuations endorsement," but the policy contains a VALUATIONS form (RM1005) and no valuations endorsement, so the cross-reference has no clear referent.

This promises up to $100,000 for the cost to "research, replace and restore lost data," whereas VALUATIONS C.4 states that the insurer will not pay any cost "including research ... of restoring or recreating lost information."
"Any substance that is hazardous to health" has no boundary at all apart from the alternative of a governmental declaration, so almost any contaminant could qualify.
This replacement gives thirty days and a $1,000,000 limit, while the unamended text of Form RM1001 D.2 still appears in the policy with a twenty-one day period and no separate limit.
This replacement gives thirty days and a $1,000,000 limit, while Form RM1001 C.3 as printed still states twenty-one days, so the policy carries both versions.
This replacement gives thirty days and a $1,000,000 limit for ingress/egress business income, while Form RM1001 C.4 as printed still states twenty-one days.

Limiting the Kansas amendments to "covered property located in Kansas" leaves the time-element coverages, which are not property located anywhere, arguably outside the endorsement even though every scheduled location is in Wichita.

The paragraph first says "either party may require that the amount be submitted for appraisal" and then says "an appraisal will be made only if both parties agree, voluntarily," two sentences that cannot both be given their natural effect.

It deletes and replaces Condition B.1 of Form RM1006, which allows either party to compel appraisal on written demand within sixty days, so whether appraisal is mandatory or consensual depends on which text controls.

The text is mutilated and breaks off mid-sentence ("Wee agreement —_ by any two (2) of these three (3) ... An appraisa p i"), so the rule on the binding effect of an appraisal award cannot be read from the provision.
It deletes and replaces Condition B.3 of Form RM1006, whose intact text makes the two-of-three written agreement conclusive as to the amount of loss.
This replaces Condition I of Form RM1006, which voids the entire policy for fraud; the two provisions attach very different consequences to the same conduct and both appear in the instrument.
The act must consist of "written statements where the known intent is to defraud," a formulation that leaves whose knowledge and intent count, and whether oral misstatements are caught, unresolved.

This five-year suit limitation replaces Condition Y of Form RM1006, which as printed requires suit within two years "or the shortest time permitted by law, whichever is greater"; the policy therefore states two limitation periods.
This ninety-day threshold replaces the sixty-day threshold in Condition F.2 of Form RM1006, which remains printed in the policy.
This substitutes a different list of cancellation grounds and notice periods for Condition F.3 of Form RM1006, which remains printed with its own, differing list.

The notice speaks of coverage "made available" and premium "shown on the DECLARATIONS," where the terrorism premium entry reads "$Declined"; read with the EXCLUSION OF CERTIFIED ACT(S) OF TERRORISM endorsement, whether any terrorism coverage exists must be inferred rather than read.

This states the cap by reference to a "calendar year" while the EXCLUSION OF CERTIFIED ACT(S) OF TERRORISM endorsement paragraph 4 states the same cap by reference to a "program year (January 1 through December 31)".
